      01

      The interruption

      Training record · medical record · product safety follow-up

      The study starts from an interruption, not from zero.

      Before April 12, the record shows a 44.00 mile high week, 12–13 mile long runs, and threshold work at 6:04–6:09 / mi. The final ten days then compressed that established fitness into shorter sharpening work. On April 12, the race itself became the interruption when the tibia fractured before the half marathon was completed.

      How?

      Mid-stride.

      The incident record reports no trip, fall, collision or external trauma. The left tibia fractured during the race and the activity ended at 7.30 miles. That is the recorded event. Why the bone failed is not resolved by this study.

      Medical finding: acute obliquely displaced fracture of the left tibial shaft. Fibula intact on the initial report.

      03

      Method / five systems

      Capacity for a lifetime

      BODY

      185 lb

      Preferred range: 180–185 lb. Body-fat aspiration: 8–10%.

      Weight trend, standardized photos, circumferences.

      Keep the fuller build while running improves. No fixed muscle-mass target and no need to force weight down to 180 lb.

      ENGINE

      Long-range aim · VO₂ 68

      Easy-running capacity, HR/pace relationship, volume tolerance.

      Current watch estimate: 51. Historical Garmin peak in the supplied export: 67 in Feb 2025. VO₂ 68 is an aspiration, not a prescription. Training does not chase the estimate. The athlete develops, and the number is allowed to follow.

      RANGE

      Strong + mobile

      A pull, a press, a hinge, a single-leg movement, calf/soleus, trunk.

      Ashtanga, Yin and core are sharpness work. Sessions are logged, not scored; one standardized mobility / trunk read every 4–6 weeks.

      PRACTICE

      A sharper daily life

      Morning pages, zazen, nutrition, sleep. Logged, not scored.

      No streaks, no discipline index. Part of the environment, not a metric to optimize.

      LONGEVITY

      More capable years

      Cardiovascular health, metabolic health, bone and muscle, mobility, cognition, recovery, connection and purpose.

      Healthspan is the frame. Performance should increase the amount of life available, not consume the life it was meant to support.

      Evidence transferability
      Ancestry informs the question. The athlete's evidence answers it.

      This athlete is Congolese, with Central African ancestry. That context matters when a reference range, prediction equation, device or published response was built from a population that may not represent him. It does not permit the study to assume a genotype, disease risk, performance trait or physiological response from ancestry alone.

      When an external norm and the athlete's repeated record disagree, first audit the source population, measurement method and model before declaring the athlete abnormal. Direct measurements and longitudinal evidence still receive clinical interpretation when appropriate. Difference is not automatically error, and individual evidence is not permission to ignore a true abnormal finding.

      Race pace logic
      Threshold establishes the ceiling. Race pace carries a durability buffer.

      The buffer is athlete-specific, not a fixed formula. A 20–30 sec / mi margin can be a useful coaching starting point, but Race Pace Durability exists to test what can actually hold over 13.1 miles. The incomplete April 12 activity does not establish that relationship for this athlete.

      Evidence

      Filed every two weeks

      Every filing follows the same grammar: BODY · ENGINE · RANGE · PRACTICE · COST · READ · NEXT. Cost and Next keep a filing from becoming a scoreboard. They record what progress took from another system and what changes because of it.

      Calendar execution surfaceGoogle Calendar mirrors the active three-week study block for running, Forge strength, fueling anchors and explicit client constraints.       Recent return contextBefore this block the athlete had already completed 6 road miles and was running more frequently. A later morning produced an unusual 2 / 10 shin signal. He stopped running for several days, increased recovery food including meat, used the elliptical, then resumed running about three days before this filing without the same issue. This is evidence of available capacity, not permission for a rapid jump.
      Cycle principleConsistency and repeatability beat catching up. A quiet day is not a lost day. The rebuild should make next week easier to execute, not make one day impressive.
      WEEK 01 · 21–27 SEPTUE 35 min easy treadmill · THU 25–30 min optional easy treadmill or rest · SAT 45 min easy treadmill.
      WEEK 02 · 28 SEP–4 OCTTUE 40 min easy treadmill · THU 30 min optional easy treadmill or rest · SAT 55 min easy treadmill.

      IntensityConversational, about RPE 2–3 / 10. Treadmill 0–0.5% incline unless comfort argues for flatter. Historical pace is evidence, not the assignment. The progression is more repeatable minutes, not faster running.
      Thursday ruleBike pacing and filming the community session are coaching work, not a speed session for the athlete. Thursday running is optional. Rest is a fully valid execution and missed minutes are not made up elsewhere.

Shorten or stop if pain becomes focal over the tibia, rises during the run, changes stride, or the next morning is clearly worse. Persistent focal pain, rest or night pain, or new swelling belongs with a clinician before more impact is added.

      Zazen10 minutes seated.
      EnvironmentRecorded as context. No streak or discipline score.
      Current operating rule · 3 weeksSmall, frequent, high-return feedings. Aim for 5–7 food exposures across the day instead of forcing large meals. Do not intentionally cut calories during the running rebuild. High-output days get more readily available carbohydrate, not a compensatory restriction later.
      Environment transitionThe old food rhythm was partly supported by spending the day at Hideout. That environment is gone, so grocery shopping, food availability and timing at home are being rebuilt at the same time as running. Treat the next three weeks as a rhythm-finding period, not proof of a permanent metabolism or permanent food list.
      Quantity vs format hypothesisThe athlete can intuitively feel under-fueled while the idea of a larger conventional meal feels aversive. Current working question: can smaller, more energy-dense feedings restore energy availability better than simply increasing meal size? Test frequency, density and timing before concluding that total food quantity alone is the problem.
      Phase-specific food ruleCurrent high-return, low-return and conditional foods describe this rebuilding phase only. Re-test later when mileage, appetite, household routine and recovery are different. A food that does little now is not permanently useless, and a food that works now is not required forever.
      Fast energy that currently worksOreos / chocolate Oreos · raisins · dried cranberries · chocolate milk. These are training-energy tools, not the whole diet. The useful question is whether they restore energy, mood and training readiness without creating a recovery cost.
      Protein laneBeef / steak · turkey · chicken · beef sticks · cottage cheese · the protein powder already on hand · eggs in moderate amounts. Working sports-nutrition reference remains 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; at 180 lb that is about 130–165 g/day. Food carries the day and powder fills gaps.
      Micronutrient / recovery laneAlmonds for a compact energy and mineral source · grapefruit and kiwi for vitamin C and fruit variety · chocolate milk and cottage cheese for protein plus calcium · beef for iron, zinc and B12. The goal is nutrient coverage around foods the athlete actually wants to repeat.
      Conditional foodsPeanuts feel useful but have sometimes produced an unwanted response. Tuna and sardines are loved but have also coincided with a facial / body response the athlete dislikes. They are not banned. Use them when presentation is not time-sensitive and observe the response rather than calling it systemic inflammation without evidence.
      Low-return foods for this phaseJasmine rice, oats, granola, chickpeas, beans, pasta, sweet potatoes, bananas and berries are not priorities. They may be eaten if wanted, but they do not currently earn a place simply because they are common endurance foods.
      Paused for nowBread, croissants, crackers and cereal have repeatedly felt poor in this environment. Avocado is paused from saturation and because it currently feels like added weight without useful return. The pause is practical, not a permanent food rule.
      Before an easy runWhen flat or underfed, test a small quick-carbohydrate feeding rather than a large meal. A current example is 3–5 Oreos 30–60 minutes before running, then file how energy, stomach and lower-leg confidence respond.
      After runningChocolate milk is the first easy recovery option. Add the protein powder when the surrounding food will not reliably cover protein. Follow with a small turkey, chicken, beef, egg or cottage-cheese feeding when appetite returns.
      Between feedingsUse almonds, raisins, dried cranberries, beef sticks, cottage cheese, grapefruit or kiwi in small portions. The system should make it easy to eat again in 2–3 hours rather than turning each feeding into a full meal.
      High-volume / presentation timingUse more of the quick-carbohydrate lane around longer running and higher-movement days. Foods that repeatedly make the face or body look disturbed belong away from coaching, filming or photography until the timing and dose are understood.
      19 SEP observationAfter the previous day's two easy runs, the athlete felt and looked flat despite having eaten. Oreos were followed by a noticeable improvement in mood plus a leaner, tighter and more vascular appearance. This is an observation, not proof of mechanism. Track whether readily available carbohydrate repeatedly produces the same response.
      Grocery list · priorityOreos / chocolate Oreos · chocolate milk · raisins · dried cranberries · almonds · steak / beef · turkey · chicken · beef sticks · cottage cheese · eggs in moderate amounts · grapefruit · kiwi. Protein powder is already on hand.
      Grocery list · conditionalPeanuts · tuna · sardines. Buy only when useful for the week and keep their response visible rather than letting them become default staples.
      Tuesday resetGrocery day is part of the study: what carried over, what ran out, what was wasted, what was actually eaten and which foods supported training without making the day harder. The food system should become easier to repeat, not more elaborate.
      Weekly rhythm readAt the Tuesday grocery reset, also ask: was food available before hunger became urgent, did the athlete avoid eating because the available option felt too large or unappealing, and did higher-output days receive enough compact carbohydrate and protein? Adjust the shopping list before adjusting discipline.
      Observation ruleWhen one food or timing change is obvious, file the food, amount, timing, activity context, energy / fullness / vascularity, facial appearance and digestion. Preserve the observation without turning one exposure into a diagnosis.
      Supplement lane · lab-gatedIron, vitamin D and B12 are not default performance stacks. Use intake plus bloodwork. Electrolyte / sodium use belongs to long or hot sessions and the athlete's sweat needs, not a daily ritual.
      DefinitionLongevity means more years with useful capacity. The study cares about healthspan, independence, mobility, cognition and the ability to keep choosing meaningful physical work. It does not use an anti-aging score.
      Cardiovascular foundationKnow resting blood pressure, lipids and aerobic capacity. A normal resting blood pressure is below 120/80 mm Hg. If readings are repeatedly elevated, confirm and manage them with a clinician rather than treating them as a training metric.
      Atherogenic riskUse the lipid panel with ApoB when available. Lp(a) is a useful once-in-adulthood inherited-risk baseline. These are health markers first, not physique markers.
      Metabolic healthFasting glucose and HbA1c sit beside waist / body-composition trend and diet quality. The goal is stable metabolic health while fuel remains sufficient for training and recovery.
      Cardiorespiratory reserveVO₂ / cardiorespiratory fitness belongs here as well as in performance. It is a capacity marker with strong long-term health relevance. The study develops the engine and lets the number follow.
      Strength reservePreserve the ability to press, pull, hinge, carry, control one leg, and produce calf / soleus force. Forge anchor lifts show whether capacity is being built or merely maintained as running returns.
      Mobility / movement freedomAshtanga, Yin and the standardized mobility / trunk read ask a longevity question too: can the athlete still access positions, control them and move through daily life without fear or unnecessary restriction?
      Bone / connective tissueProgressive loading, adequate energy and nutrient sufficiency are part of the rebuild. The April fracture stays a medical fact, not a theory. Any deeper bone-health evaluation or bone-density testing is clinician-directed when indicated.
      Sleep / recoveryMost adults need about 7–9 hours of sleep. Sleep is treated as part of cardiovascular, cognitive and training health. The study records useful context rather than awarding sleep points.
      Preventive careKeep primary-care review, dental and vision care, vaccinations and age / risk-appropriate screening current. The study can record completion dates, but it does not replace preventive medicine.
      Connection / purposeMeaningful work, relationships, community and activities worth waking up for belong in a longevity study. Morning pages and the Read filing capture direction without turning purpose into a numerical score.
      Quality-of-life questionEvery filing asks: Is training expanding the life or shrinking it? Can the athlete do more, recover better, move with more freedom, remain present to people and work, and still have reserve for difficult things?
      DirectionPerformance is not the destination. It gives the body direction and proof. Health protects the years, mobility gives access to them, performance creates capacity inside them, and purpose decides what that capacity is for.
      Athlete contextCongolese / Central African ancestry. This is a transferability flag, not a physiological verdict. The study does not convert ancestry into assumptions about genotype, ability, disease or response.
      Evidence hierarchyRepeated athlete data → direct laboratory / clinical measurement → evidence from a closely matched population → broad population norms → wearable or prediction-model estimate. A lower rung can inform a higher one, but should not silently overrule it.
      Source auditWhen a result matters, ask: who was studied, where, age and sex distribution, training status, ancestry representation, assay or device, and whether the equation was validated outside its original sample.
      Do not flatten AfricaAfrican ancestry is not one biological category. Central, West, East, North and Southern African populations can differ substantially, and country or region still does not substitute for an individual's measurements.
      CBC / ANCIf absolute neutrophil count is repeatedly below a laboratory reference while the athlete is otherwise well, consider Duffy-null associated neutrophil count as one possible explanation and discuss Duffy testing with a clinician. Do not infer Duffy status from ancestry alone.
      Kidney functionUse current race-free CKD-EPI eGFR reporting. When creatinine-based eGFR is discordant with the clinical picture or precision matters, cystatin C can provide a useful second filtration marker.
      Lung functionIf spirometry is ever used, prefer current race-neutral interpretation rather than older race-specific corrections. Report the raw measurements and the reference equation used.
      Optical sensorsPulse oximetry and other optical signals can have accuracy differences across skin pigmentation. Treat an implausible SpO₂ or optical wearable result as something to confirm, especially when it conflicts with symptoms or a direct measurement.
      Athlete heartIf ECG or echocardiography ever enters the study, use athlete-specific interpretation with sports-cardiology expertise. Recent elite-football data show that cardiac adaptation can vary even among Black athletes by regional ancestry, including Central African groups. That finding is context for interpretation, not evidence that this athlete has an abnormality.
      Wearables / algorithmsGarmin VO₂, body-composition devices, recovery scores and future prediction models are estimates. Where a model's validation population is unclear, label its transferability uncertain and compare it against direct testing before using it to change the program.
      Conflict ruleWhen a population norm conflicts with repeated individual evidence, do not force the athlete to fit the norm. Re-measure, check the method, use a better reference or direct test, and involve a clinician where the finding could represent disease.
      Reusable coaching ruleThis lens applies to every athlete, not only this one. The goal is not ancestry-based programming. The goal is to know when a scientific result travels well and when uncertainty should remain visible.
      BASELINE · bloodworkDo once now if practical: CBC with differential · ferritin · serum iron + TIBC / transferrin · transferrin saturation · B12 · folate · CMP · fasting glucose · HbA1c · lipid panel · ApoB · Lp(a) · TSH · 25-OH vitamin D. hs-CRP is optional context, not a score.
      Collection standardPrefer a morning draw. Arrive well hydrated, without acute illness. Keep the prior 24 hours low to moderate and avoid muscle-damaging training for 2–3 days when the goal is a clean iron / recovery baseline. Follow the lab's fasting instructions for tests that require it.
      What not to chaseHematocrit and hemoglobin are observations, not performance targets. Read them with ferritin, transferrin saturation, hydration, plasma-volume effects and the rest of the CBC. A higher hematocrit is not automatically a better athlete.
      Repeat ruleIf iron status is normal and the athlete is well, recheck around 6 months or before a major high-volume / altitude block. If iron depletion, symptoms or high-risk conditions appear, repeat timing becomes clinician-directed and may be more frequent. Broad health markers are normally annual unless a result changes the question. Lp(a) is generally a once-in-adulthood baseline unless a clinician gives a reason to repeat it.
      Bloodwork · practical Miami pathQuest Diagnostics · University of Miami ↗, 1050 NW 14th St, Suite 110. Quest accepts clinician orders and eligible self-purchased testing. Labcorp OnDemand ↗ is the second simple path with digital results and direct-purchase panels.
      VO₂ · gate before the testDo not schedule a maximal test because the page wants a number. Open the gate when the tibia / lower leg is cleared for maximal graded exercise, easy running is stable, faster running can be introduced without a next-day flare, and the chosen modality can represent the athlete. For a runner, prefer a treadmill protocol when available.
      VO₂ · first optionUHealth Fitness & Wellness Center ↗, 1120 NW 14th St, 9th Floor. University of Miami has published VO₂ testing through this system. Confirm current VO₂ / CPET availability and whether the test can be treadmill-based before booking.
      VO₂ · nearby backupInfinity Delta ↗, 310 NE 61st St. Current listings include VO₂max and RMR testing. Useful if proximity makes repeat testing easier.
      VO₂ · performance-lab backupP2 Performance Lab ↗, 12511 S Dixie Hwy. VO₂max, lactate, gait, force plates and return-to-performance testing live in one place. This is the option when the question expands beyond one aerobic number.
      VO₂ · study cadenceFirst lab value after the gate opens. Re-test after a meaningful aerobic block, usually 8–12 weeks, or at a major phase transition when the result could change training. Do not test monthly just to create a graph.
      Optional testsRMR is useful if calorie needs remain unclear after 2–3 weeks of intake + weight + training evidence. DEXA can serve as an occasional body-composition anchor. Gait / force-plate work belongs later, when the limb can safely be challenged and the result will change running or strength decisions.

      Baseline exampleStrength and faster running waited while the tibia governed.
      RuleA gain is not automatically a win if another system becomes unstable.

      Current stateTuesday and Saturday are the running anchors. Thursday remains optional after bike-led coaching. Non-running cross-training is fixed: Monday bike after Hinge, Wednesday elliptical after Thrust, Friday bike after Lower Pump + Core. Historical pace does not set the current prescription.

      Read & next

      A paragraph, not a score

      What's changing? What feels alive? What feels forced? What am I becoming interested in? Is training expanding the life or shrinking it? Not "energy 7/10." An actual note is filed alongside the numbers because the point was never just the body.

      Cost: what this fortnight's progress took from another system. Sometimes nothing. Sometimes "strength waited for the tibia."

      Next: what changes because of what was just filed. Sometimes: continue, no change.

      Follow the study as it happens.

      New evidence filed roughly every two weeks: standardized photos, training receipts, an updated read. Nothing is edited out after the fact.
